claims.statement: By 14 March 2025, Mój Prąd 6.0 had received more than 104,000 applications, and NFOŚiGW reported that more than 40% of applications taken up for assessment were returned for correction or completion; this establishes frequent documentation rework in that program, but not who bore the cost.

Mój Prąd 6.0 required multiple non-editable attachments; absence of the OSD certificate caused rejection without review of the remaining documents, while a missing or incorrectly completed acceptance protocol for an energy or heat store could require correction and the installer's own protocol template was not accepted.

The Mój Prąd application window cited by the candidate ran from 2 September 2024 to 12 September 2025 and is closed, so its precise packet cannot be treated as a current or permanent recurring demand source.

Polish household-renewables subsidy paperwork continued after Mój Prąd: the transitional Przydomowe Magazyny Energii intake had 12,738 applications by 8 May 2026, reopened in June, and a Fundusz Modernizacyjny successor was planned for Q3 2026; continuity of events is evidenced, but the governing program and eligibility rules change.

The planned PME 2 workflow requires the currently valid OSD certificate and acceptance-protocol templates, replacement of an old certificate where required fields changed, and device and nameplate photos; the program page also says submitted photos will be automatically checked for editing.

TAURON's microinstallation process requires customer and site identifiers, equipment data, an installer declaration, an electrical diagram and sometimes technical sheets and certificates; TAURON verifies the submission and allows up to 30 days after receipt of a complete filing to install or configure metering, so the DSO rather than a passport vendor controls grid acceptance.

Reonic already markets to renewable installers a mobile and offline-capable installation workflow with configurable checklists, photo documentation, digital signatures, project documentation and automatically generated PDF handover reports, closely overlapping the proposed capture and handover artifact.

SMA offers installers a manufacturer-specific app that commissions compatible inverter, meter and battery systems, sets grid codes, registers monitoring and claims a five-to-ten-minute setup, demonstrating a credible OEM bundling route for the device-commissioning portion of the job.

Fronius warranty terms require the warranty holder to supply a commissioning protocol, invoice with serial number, legible rating-plate photo and further requested information, after which Fronius decides the warranty service in its sole discretion; a third-party passport does not itself control warranty recognition.

EU Commission guidance permits an external service provider to process personal data for an installer-controller when a binding controller-processor contract exists and the processor provides specified guarantees, follows documented instructions and implements security measures; this makes a lawful contractual path possible but creates onboarding and compliance work.

A Polish photovoltaic wholesaler publicly offers installers a per-install OSD-filing service under a framework agreement for 145.53 PLN net (179 PLN gross), using end-customer powers and forms and promising completed documentation within three working days; however, the page was marked unavailable and showed zero product reviews at access, so it is an offer and price anchor, not verified sales volume.

URE recorded 1,636,673 Polish renewable microinstallations at the end of 2025 and reported that 99.9% were photovoltaic; this is a large installed base but does not measure annual commissioning-passport events or the number of target installer accounts.

URE reported that annual growth in the number of microinstallations slowed from about 41% in 2022 to 15% in 2023 and 10% in 2024, cautioning against extrapolating the installed base into rapidly growing new-installation volume.

No executed installer workflow-integration agreement, data-processing agreement, pilot commitment, or authority to make passport completion a mandatory handover checkpoint is available in the evidence packet.

It is unknown whether Polish small installers will pay 120-250 PLN for this standalone passport plus a 300-900 PLN monthly account fee, whether they will pay repeatedly, or whether the homeowner rather than the installer captures most of the subsidy benefit.

There is no measured evidence for acquisition cost, sales conversion, passports per installer, crew onboarding time, capture completion, OCR accuracy, manual-exception rate, support burden, storage and security cost, churn, cash collection, or fully loaded contribution margin.

No evidence establishes that an NFOŚiGW program, DSO, equipment OEM, insurer, lender, distributor or homeowner will contractually recognize this passport as satisfying its acceptance, payment or warranty gate.
Crew compliance with an additional capture workflow and generalization from a family-firm pilot to unrelated installers remain unmeasured.

There is no evidence that the venture can lawfully retain enough de-identified exception data, obtain enough volume, or derive a predictive advantage that competitors cannot reproduce from public rules and their own installer workflows.

A cross-brand completeness layer could reduce preventable packet errors, but because official current forms and third-party-issued certificates remain mandatory, its artifact would supplement rather than replace the documents or the external acceptance decision.

Because an all-in-one installer platform can already bundle nearly identical evidence capture and handover reports, an OEM can bundle device commissioning, and a wholesaler can sell completed filings, the proposed product needs demonstrably superior cross-brand rule maintenance, integration or recognized acceptance rather than a useful PDF alone.

The adjacent Alians price sits inside the candidate's proposed per-passport range while including actual preparation and delivery to institutions, so it is evidence of a competitive price anchor but not evidence that a validation-only passport can sustain the same price or the candidate's target margin.

contrary_evidence: The cited Mój Prąd 6.0 intake closed on 12 September 2025 and was followed by transitional and successor programs with changed eligibility, required fields and official templates, making static rule coverage fragile.

Reonic already provides digital checklists, mobile and offline photo capture, signatures and automatically generated PDF handover reports, so the core artifact can be bundled into a broader installer system.
SMA already bundles rapid device commissioning and monitoring registration for its own equipment, giving OEM software a privileged substitute position for part of the workflow.
Fronius, not a third-party passport provider, specifies its required warranty evidence and retains discretion over warranty service; no contractual recognition of the passport is shown.

A Polish wholesaler advertises completed OSD-filing work at 145.53 PLN net, inside the proposed passport price range; the candidate may compete against a service that performs more of the actual administrative outcome.
The Alians offer was unavailable and had zero displayed reviews, so a posted adjacent price cannot be mistaken for verified transaction volume or repeat demand.
URE's large installed-base figure does not reveal eligible new commissioning density, and the regulator documented a substantial deceleration in annual microinstallation growth through 2024.

unknowns: Whether any installer will execute the proposed 12-month workflow-integration and data-processing agreement and actually enforce the passport before customer handover.
How often incomplete documentation creates installer-paid rework, delayed installer collections, uncompensated callbacks or lost warranty recovery, rather than costs borne by homeowners or advisers.
Whether small Polish installers will pay the stated per-passport and monthly prices for validation without the vendor itself submitting to the DSO, subsidy administrator or OEM.
Whether the family-firm pilot will generalize to unrelated installers and whether a distributor or software partner will sign a measurable referral or integration agreement.
Crew completion rate, time added per job, exception frequency, OCR accuracy, manual-review minutes, support load and security overhead.
Fully loaded CAC, gross contribution per passport, account churn, payment timing and payback period.
Whether authorities, DSOs, OEMs, insurers or lenders will recognize the passport in an approval, payment or warranty decision.
Whether consented and de-identified exception data can be retained at sufficient scale and can create a defensible advantage beyond public rules and incumbent workflow data.
